Get started

Write your first script

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Define the script stateBuild the projectAttach the script and runAdd the next piece

This example attaches a compiled Odin script to a Node2D and moves it every frame. Start with the SDK installed and a project whose extension and build helpers are wired as described in the project setup.

Define the script state#

Create scripts/mover.odin. Use the same package name as the project's other scripts; the example below uses my_game_scripts.

Odin
//gd:extends Node2D
//gd:class Mover
package my_game_scripts

import gd "godot:godot"

Mover :: struct {
    owner: gd.Node2d,
    speed: f32 `gd:"export,default=120"`,
}

mover_ready :: proc(self: ^Mover) {
    gd.print("Mover ready!")
}

mover_process :: proc(self: ^Mover, delta: f64) {
    position := gd.node2d_get_position(self.owner)
    position.x += self.speed * f32(delta)
    gd.node2d_set_position(self.owner, position)
}

owner is the engine node. self points to the Odin struct. Pass self.owner when an engine function asks for a node; pass self to your own procedures that operate on the script state.

The gd:"export" tag makes Speed editable in the Inspector. The mover_ prefix associates the procedures with Mover; Godot sees the usual _ready and _process callbacks through generated registration.

Build the project#

From an SDK development shell, pass the project directory to the build helper:

Shell
bash build/build_scripts.sh /absolute/path/to/your_game

For an installed addon, use its helper and prebuilt core as shown in existing project setup.

The build runs scriptgen and compiles authored and generated source together. Generated *.gen.odin files are build outputs; edit the authored script instead.

Attach the script and run#

Open the project, add a Node2D, and attach res://scripts/mover.odin in its Script slot. Speed should appear in the Inspector with a default of 120. Run the scene: the Output panel prints the ready message and the node moves right.

Change Speed in the Inspector, then change the procedure and rebuild. This separates authored scene values from compiled behavior and gives you a small scene for checking the edit/build/run loop.

Add the next piece#

Use the authoring reference for typed signals, Godot-callable methods, Resource fields, and on-ready node lookup. The script model explains shared data, cross-script access, and composition. For input, movement, combat, or networking, choose a runnable example close to your game.
